page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a title heading at the top and an italic verse poem below it. No margin notes. The page opens a division, so there is no running head.

main_text.l: in loco constructo, ubi prius martyres

l.i: Hic ubi concursu populus noua
templa frequentat,
Et psalmis mixtas tollit in alta preces,
Laudantisq; Deum dependet ab ore ministri,
Terribilis nuper carnificina fuit.
Qua tot Christiada miseranda sorte beatas
Et ferro, & flammis depofuere animas.
Quàm male cæca Deo mens ultrò humana resistit!
Nilque ratum, nisi quod concipit, esse putat!
Namq; ubi nulla truces satiabat poena Tyrannos
In Christi famulos qui fera bella gerunt:
Templa Deo surgunt notas resonantia laudes
Quas plebs ingenti maxima voce canit.
F-
alleris ô qui bella moues, qui excindere tepla hac, [?]
Et Christo addictum vis abolere genus,
In noua, non cernis? cineres sunt corpora versi,
Ossaque in innumeros sunt renouata viros?
Inspersus cineri sanguis redivivus in auras
Surgit, & authorem prædicat usque suum.

page.notes: Ornamental strip below the page number and the woodcut initial H were not transcribed as text beyond the letter H, which is joined to "Hic". Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so "Ossaque" and "Inspersus" are read from the long-s forms and the reading is not certain at the final letter. "tepla" is printed as shown and is probably a misprint for "templa"; marked [?]. The verse lines are italic and each printed line is given as its own paragraph because the poem has no stanza breaks. Faint show-through from the reverse side on the right edge was ignored.
